answer: A market for basalt and ferrous scrap admits agents through secure hardware. Each chip signs the epoch nonce and agent key, with a manufacturer certificate for a unique device identifier. Validators verify both signatures and reserve that identifier for one seat per epoch; another key using it is rejected. A hollow software clone lacks the chip secret. Every extra alias therefore needs another genuine device, even in parallel, and an old signature fails the fresh nonce. Security assumes unextractable keys and an honest issuer that cannot mint cheap certificates.
